Mo and W were enriched at the grain boundaries on the annealed surface, and Zr and Si were enriched to form sphere-shaped silicides, as marked by circles in the STEM micrograph, Fig. 4 (a), and EDS map, Fig. 4 (b).
After annealing at 650 ◦ C for 3 h, sub-grains with a diameter of about 500 nm are generated, as shown in Fig. 8 (d).
Within the α -grain matrix, numerous dislocation walls (marked by red arrows) are formed, resulting in a well-organized dislocation structure.

Additionally, deformed twins are evident in Fig. 8 (c).

Silicides are generated in the vicinity of the surface region due to the relatively high dislocation density on the surface after the rolling process. The room temperature ductility can be restored by removing the near-surface area.

the microstructure evolution during high-temperature tensile deformation is closely related to dynamic recrystallization in the whole sample, which contributes to the refinement of grains and reduction in deformation resistance and enhances the alloy ’ s ductility
The high strength of the as-received BTi6431S alloy is rooted in the high dislocation density and collective dislocation behavior in the α phase.
